description: Complete verification against original material (verifier-toolkit/1 §8.5): the verifier holds the original material and confirms it matches the certificate's committed subjects. For each subject it recomputes canonical_bytes(subject) under the declared profile, derives the verifier-local subject_local_digest_hex = SHA3-256(canonical_bytes), and rebuilds the CCCP/1 commitment SHA3-256(ASCII(nonce_hex) || ASCII(subject_local_digest_hex)); it MUST equal the certificate's commitment_digest_hex. For subject.collection/1, it also reconstructs the collection root from the ordered leaves under collection.merkle-sha3-256/1 and requires the leaf count to equal declared_cardinality. This pins the bytes so any toolkit in any language detects a volume/cardinality lie identically (the volume-fairness check of verifier-toolkit/1 §8.5.3, for subjects declared as collections).
canonicalization: subject.binary/1 = exact input bytes (opaque). subject.collection/1 = RFC 8785 JCS of the collection JSON object. collection.merkle-sha3-256/1 leaf_preimage = utf8('CERTCRYPT:collection.merkle-sha3-256/1:leaf') || u64be(len(collection_salt_bytes)) || collection_salt_bytes || u64be(len(leaf_profile_bytes)) || leaf_profile_bytes || u64be(len(leaf_canonical_bytes)) || leaf_canonical_bytes, where collection_salt_bytes = ASCII(nonce_hex) (subject.collection/1 §8) ; node_preimage = utf8('CERTCRYPT:collection.merkle-sha3-256/1:node') || left_hash || right_hash (32 raw bytes each). DISTINCT from the settlement Merkle (0x00/0x01 prefixes) — MUST NOT substitute.
commitment_construction: commitment_digest_hex = SHA3-256(ASCII(nonce_hex) || ASCII(subject_local_digest_hex)); all hex lowercase, ASCII concatenation of the hex strings (not the binary digests). subject_local_digest_hex is verifier-local and MUST NOT be published — it is pinned here only as a conformance check value.

subjects.note: opaque binary subject: canonical_bytes = exact input bytes
collection of 3 binary leaves; root reconstructed under collection.merkle-sha3-256/1; declared_cardinality MUST equal the leaf count (3)

negative_cases.name: cardinality lie
negative_cases.scenario: declared_cardinality='4' but only 3 leaves delivered (or vice versa)
negative_cases.why: leaf count that participated in the root != declared_cardinality

negative_cases.name: tampered leaf
negative_cases.scenario: one leaf material altered by a byte

negative_cases.name: tampered binary subject
negative_cases.scenario: binary subject material altered by a byte

negative_cases.name: wrong merkle scheme substituted
negative_cases.scenario: settlement Merkle (0x00/0x01) used instead of collection.merkle-sha3-256/1

negative_cases.name: empty collection
negative_cases.why: empty tree is invalid under collection.merkle-sha3-256/1 §12.4

must_hold: subject.collection/1 canonical_bytes is RFC 8785 JCS of the collection object (keys sorted: commitment_scheme, declared_cardinality, leaves, root)
collection leaf/node preimage use domain tags + u64be big-endian length prefixes (NOT the settlement 0x00/0x01 prefixes)
the collection root is reconstructed from the ordered leaves; single leaf -> its own hash; odd width -> promote lone right-edge hash unchanged
leaf count that participated in the root MUST equal declared_cardinality (volume-fairness check, verifier-toolkit/1 §8.5.3)
commitment = SHA3-256(ASCII(nonce_hex) || ASCII(subject_local_digest_hex)), all lowercase hex, ASCII of the hex strings
subject_local_digest_hex is verifier-local and never published in a certificate
